title: Police investigated in death of homeless man
article: --- _TORONTO_ - City _police_ officers are under investigation to see if they caused injuries which may have contributed to the _death_ of a homeless man.

The Special Investigations Unit, which investigates _deaths_ or serious injuries involving _police_, has been piecing together the whereabouts of Stuart _Mitchell_ in the seven hours after _police_ detained him on Jan. _30_.
They're investigating whether chest injuries sustained by _Mitchell_ may have stemmed from a run-in with _police_.
A friend of _Mitchell_'s told the _Toronto_ Star that two cops "jumped" on his chest that night while another female cop told them to "take it easy."
_Mitchell_, 49, was admitted to a local hospital Jan. 31, complaining of chest pain. Nineteen days later, following a transfer to another hospital, he died.
The SIU is not releasing autopsy results.
Investigators have learned that _Mitchell_ was briefly detained by officers who responded to a gun call at a downtown rooming house about 11:_30_ p.m.
No gun was found on _Mitchell_, who was released about _30_ minutes later.

On Wednesday, the Special Investigations Unit confirmed _Mitchell_ was involved with _police_ Jan. _30_. The agency asked for the public's help to determine what happened to _Mitchell_ from the time _police_ released him at midnight to his arrival at a hostel the next morning.
_Mitchell_ told several people "he had been assaulted by _Toronto_ _police_ officers on the night of _January_ _30_, _2000_," the SIU said.
_Mitchell_'s older brother, Bob, said _Mitchell_ was a father of three who had worked hard until a few years ago when he suffered from an industrial accident and the _death_ of their brother in 1993.
"I often thought he wouldn't last long in life," said his brother, 53, who works in the music industry.
